identification.summary: CL-STA-0048 is a temporary cluster name used by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 for a cyber-espionage cluster active since May 2024 against South Asian telecommunications organizations and government agencies, which Unit 42 reported on 2025-01-29 and assessed to be of Chinese origin [S1][S2][S4]. EclecticIQ later listed CL-STA-0048 among Chinese clusters it linked to exploitation of SAP NetWeaver CVE-2025-31324 [S3][S5].
identification.firstObserved: Unit 42 timeline begins May 2024; report published 2025-01-29 [S1][S2].
identification.notes: CL-STA-0048 is a Unit 42 'CL-STA' (cluster, state-aligned) designation, not a Microsoft name; no Microsoft mapping or MITRE group ID is cited here. Do not merge with CL-STA-0969 (a separate Unit 42 cluster targeting Southeast/Southwest Asian telecoms) [S2]. The SAP NetWeaver link is EclecticIQ's tradecraft-based assessment, not confirmed technical overlap [S3][S5].

attribution.sponsor: Suspected China-nexus; no specific PRC agency is named in the sources gathered [S1][S2].
attribution.confidence: Unit 42 assessed moderate-to-high confidence that the activity has a Chinese nexus, per secondary coverage of its report [S1][S2].
attribution.basis: Per secondary coverage, Unit 42 based its assessment on tools, TTPs, infrastructure and victimology [S1][S2]. EclecticIQ's later linkage of CL-STA-0048 to SAP NetWeaver exploitation rests on analyst tradecraft assessment [S3][S5].

objectives: Espionage: Unit 42 characterizes the activity as an espionage operation against high-value targets in South Asia, with secondary coverage describing a goal of stealing sensitive and personal information with a focus on government employees [S1][S2][S4].

targeting.notes: Telecommunications organizations and government agencies in South Asia [S1][S2][S4]. EclecticIQ's SAP NetWeaver reporting covers the combined set of Chinese clusters, not CL-STA-0048 specifically [S3][S5].

capabilities.summary: Per Unit 42 coverage, initial access via exploitation of vulnerabilities in IIS, Apache Tomcat and MSSQL services [S2][S4]. Living-off-the-land binaries (certutil) used to deploy PlugX in memory; hex staging used to deliver a Cobalt Strike beacon, which was injected into an SQL server process and used to bring in tunneling tools (Stowaway and iox, per one search summary) [S2]. Data exfiltrated over DNS; a new SQL database user was created for persistence and database queries; PowerShell used for enumeration [S2][S4]. Secondary profiles describe DNS exfiltration triggered by ping commands [S4]. In the SAP NetWeaver context, EclecticIQ reports CL-STA-0048 used the vulnerability to create a reverse shell to a previously used IP address [S3][S5].

campaigns.name: South Asia telecom and government espionage
campaigns.summary: Start of the activity timeline Unit 42 documents (May 2024 to November 2024) against telecommunications organizations and government agencies in South Asia [S1][S2][S4].

campaigns.name: Unit 42 public report
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 publishes 'CL-STA-0048: An Espionage Operation Against High-Value Targets in South Asia' [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: SAP NetWeaver CVE-2025-31324 exploitation
campaigns.summary: Critical unauthenticated file-upload flaw in SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer exploited in the wild; Help Net Security reported exploitation on 2025-04-28 [S6]. EclecticIQ assessed with high confidence that activity began in April 2025 [S5].

campaigns.name: EclecticIQ links Chinese clusters to SAP exploitation
campaigns.summary: EclecticIQ, from an exposed attacker open directory, linked intrusions to UNC5221, UNC5174 and CL-STA-0048; the directory held a file recording 581 compromised NetWeaver instances (attacker's own tally, not independently verified) [S3][S5].

diamond.adversary: Suspected China-nexus cluster; sponsor not specified in cited sources [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Exploitation of IIS, Apache Tomcat and MSSQL; certutil, PlugX, Cobalt Strike, hex staging, DNS exfiltration, SQL persistence [S2][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: C2 servers receiving exfiltrated SQL data and Cobalt Strike traffic; reverse shell to a previously used IP in the SAP context [S3][S4]. Specific indicators were not verified from the primary report.
diamond.victim: South Asian telecommunications organizations and government agencies [S1][S2][S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Espionage collection against government and telecom data in South Asia consistent with a Chinese-nexus assessment [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing IIS, Apache Tomcat, MSSQL and (per EclecticIQ) SAP NetWeaver servers [S2][S3][S5].

gaps: The Unit 42 primary report could not be opened (host unreachable from this environment); details come from search summaries and secondary coverage and should be validated against the primary [S1][S2].
The EclecticIQ primary report could not be opened; SAP linkage details come from press coverage [S3][S5].
Exact date of the IMDA advisory not seen; date given is approximate.
Stowaway/iox and ping-based DNS beaconing were reported in only some summaries and are unverified against the primary.
Specific victim organizations and countries, exact CVEs used for IIS/Tomcat/MSSQL access, and C2 indicators are not confirmed.
No Microsoft actor name, MITRE group ID, or overlap with other named China-nexus groups confirmed; no activity after 2025-05 sourced.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing web and database servers (IIS, Tomcat, MSSQL, SAP NetWeaver) at telecom and government organizations are key cyber terrain [S2][S3]. STEP 2: Exploitation of known, unpatched services and living-off-the-land tooling reduce defender visibility [S2][S4]. STEP 3: Template is public-facing exploit, certutil/hex-staged PlugX and Cobalt Strike, tunneling, SQL-based collection, DNS exfiltration [S2][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage against South Asian telecom and government networks. MDCOA is use of telecom footholds to reach downstream government or partner data, or rapid exploitation of the next enterprise-server CVE (as with SAP). Candidate indicators: new SQL users, certutil decoding hex files, Cobalt Strike injected into SQL server processes, anomalous DNS or ping-based traffic [S2][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track patch status of internet-facing IIS, Tomcat, MSSQL and SAP systems across supported and partner networks in South Asia [S2][S3]. (2) Authorities: telecom and host-nation networks are outside DODIN authorities; coordinate through partner-nation and information-sharing channels. (3) Mission assurance: telecom dependencies for regional operations warrant contingency comms planning. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3 and allies; attribution is a vendor assessment and may shift, so prioritize containment [S1][S3].
